trust_decision.summary: Under channelBinding=require the driver decides that the SCRAM handshake must complete with a -PLUS (tls-server-end-point) mechanism and must never silently continue with plain SCRAM; that decision is made in ScramAuthenticator when the channel-binding data is derived from the peer certificate (empty for hash-less signature algorithms such as Ed25519) and when the scram-client builder silently selects a non-PLUS mechanism.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names unsupported certificate signature algorithms; an engineer reading only the summary goes to the one call that turns the peer certificate into channel-binding data, sees that its byte[] result is passed straight into the ScramClient builder (line 61) and produces no error when empty.

fix_sites.entry_point: Connection establishment with channelBinding=require: java.sql.DriverManager.getConnection / Driver.connect / javax.sql.DataSource.getConnection -> ConnectionFactoryImpl.doAuthentication (AUTH_REQ_SASL, ConnectionFactoryImpl.java:997-1022) -> new ScramAuthenticator -> initializeScramClient
fix_sites.module_kind: core library, SCRAM negotiation layer (post-condition on the mechanism chosen by the third-party scram-client builder)

fix_sites.entry_point: Same connection-establishment call chain; here the certificate-to-hash derivation helper getChannelBindingData
fix_sites.module_kind: core library, certificate/TLS data-derivation helper (private lower-level static method)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advertised-mechanism gate already rejects servers that offer no -PLUS mechanism (ScramAuthenticator.java:89-95), and a real PostgreSQL server only advertises the -PLUS name the driver can actually negotiate, so a post-check on the negotiated mechanism looks like redundant defence-in-depth rather than a different route: the library silently chooses plain SCRAM and the driver's own suffix test is what let it through.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: channelBinding=prefer is the default (PGProperty.java:157) and must keep connecting to TLS servers whose certificate yields no channel-binding hash (silently using plain SCRAM) and to non-TLS servers; channelBinding=disable must short-circuit before any certificate work. An over-broad fix that throws whenever the derived channel-binding data is empty, or that rejects an empty peer-certificate list unconditionally, breaks the default mode and every plaintext SCRAM connection.

O6_input_shapes: channel-binding data derived from the certificate: non-empty for RSA/ECDSA signatures vs empty byte[] for hash-less algorithms (Ed25519 / OID 1.3.101.112) under RFC 5929
no peer certificate array or a peer Certificate that is not an X509Certificate, which also falls through to an empty byte[]
no TLS at all: the socket is a plain Socket rather than an SSLSocket
the negotiated mechanism is a -PLUS mechanism vs a plain SCRAM-SHA-256 mechanism that the client library selected
the channelBinding setting itself: require (must throw) vs prefer/disable (must continue to connect)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Under channelBinding=require, an empty or non-X509 peer certificate array falls through to the trailing 'return new byte[0]' with no error; the published fix added its REQUIRE throw only inside the X509Certificate branch, so this input shape is closed only by the separate mechanism post-check rather than at the derivation site.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: JSSE throws SSLPeerUnverifiedException when the session has no peer certificates and TLS peers always present X.509 certificates, so the branch is unreachable in practice; a solver fixing only the Ed25519 case can argue it out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same function, 30 lines below the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Validate that the mechanism the client finally selects was actually advertised and is negotiable by this client, not merely a name ending in -PLUS
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainers already hand-roll wire-level SCRAM checks here after being burned twice by the third-party scram library, so a local 'mechanism must match what we can use' guard is exactly the kind of code they would add next to the existing name-suffix test.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Extend the channelBinding=require fail-closed checks to the SCRAM-completion state (e.g. require that the GS2 channel-binding flag actually sent in the client-first message was 'p' and that the handshake that finished is the one that started with a PLUS mechanism)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: That block is where every channelBinding=require rejection for non-SASL / skipped authentication already lives, so a maintainer hardening the same property would add the next case there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A PGStream accessor for the negotiated SSLSession / peer certificate that applies the same fail-closed rule when TLS state is missing or unexpected
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: PGStream owns the socket and its changeSocket layer, so any TLS state the authenticator needs is naturally exposed through it; a fix author avoiding 'instanceof SSLSocket' in the authenticator would put the check here.

O9_family: fail-open on a negotiated security mechanism: CWE-636 (not failing securely) and CWE-757 (selection of a less secure algorithm during negotiation), i.e. silent channel-binding authentication downgrade
